messages:
sarah.ae: Hey team — AtlasHealth POC kickoff tomorrow. Customer asks for a connectivity checklist: they want LLM inference in our Private VPC, traffic from their on‑prem to our model nodes, and crucially they need source IP preservation for downstream logging. Also security questionnaire expects specific firewall rules + SOC2/FIPS note. Can we confirm options + any blockers?

kyle-net: @sarah.ae quick summary of options: 1) VPC Peering (cross-account, simple; will NAT on our side if using NAT gateway — loses srcip unless we use proxy). 2) Interface endpoints / PrivateLink (TLS, per-service ENIs, easier audit). 3) Transit Gateway (recommended for multi-VPC/multi-account). For src-ip preservation: we can preserve client IP if traffic flows directly to customer-managed proxy in their VPC or if we terminate on GWLB+proxy that forwards original src via proxy protocol.

maria-se: Pricing/POC note: Private deployment (VPC mode) has platform fee + infra. If they need NAT-free srcip preservation we may need dedicated egress IPs or a BYO-proxy design — that affects setup time (add ~2-4 business days) and possibly adds a small engineering handoff fee. I'll include a short estimate in the POC quote.

ida-security: Security constraints: they requested SOC2 + FIPS mention in the questionnaire. We are SOC2 compliant (link: https://redwood.example.com/compliance) and our Private package supports customer KMS/HSM for keys to help with FIPS requirements. For firewall rules please provide a minimal allowed list so security can sign off.

kyle-net: Minimal network checklist (customer -> Redwood Private):
- Allow outbound TCP 443 to our ingestion ENIs (example 10.20.50.0/26).
- Allow inbound ephemeral return traffic (1024-65535) if you're doing stateful NAT on-prem.
- For mutual TLS handshakes allow 443 and 8443 depending on plan.
- If using interface endpoints, allow SGs to this interface only.

ops-bot: Sample firewall snippet (ACL / security team friendly):

```
# Allow traffic from customer on-prem to Redwood model endpoints (example)
ALLOW TCP 443 FROM 198.51.100.0/24 TO 10.20.50.0/26   # REDWOOD-INGEST-ENIS
ALLOW TCP 8443 FROM 198.51.100.0/24 TO 10.20.50.0/26   # ALTERNATE TLS PORT
# Ephemeral return ports (if no proxy translation)
ALLOW TCP 1024-65535 FROM 10.20.50.0/26 TO 198.51.100.0/24
# Optional: healthchecks from our infra
ALLOW TCP 443 FROM 172.31.10.8/32 TO 198.51.100.10/32  # health-checker
```

kyle-net: If they absolutely need straight-through src-ip on the model instance (no proxy header), the only safe pattern is: customer connects to a customer-owned proxy in the same VPC as the model instances (or we co-locate a dedicated proxy with preserved source set to forward). That is an architecture we can implement under Private but it's a bit higher ops.

maria-se: POC scope options (short):
- Quick option (fastest): Interface endpoint + standard SGs. Pros: minimal config, no infra handoff. Cons: srcip will be the interface ENI unless customer terminates proxy.
- Medium: Transit-GW peering + TGW attachment to our VPC, route propagation. Pros: scales to many accounts. Cons: takes TGW approval + routing work.
- Full preserved-srcip: BYO Proxy or dedicated GWLB+proxy flow. Pros: meets logging/forensics. Cons: setup time + dedicated egress IPs.

ida-security: For questionnaire items 3.2/3.3 (network isolation + egress control) we can provide: a one-page network diagram, the SG/ACL snippet above, and a stmt about KMS keys. I'll need the final CIDR they plan to connect from to complete the doc.

sarah.ae: Thanks — Atlas says they can give two static source /24s: 198.51.100.0/24 and 198.51.101.0/24. They prefer preserved srcip for security logging. Next steps?

kyle-net: With those CIDRs we can draft SG rules. Quick ask: do they have a preferred pattern: peer-to-peer (VPC peering) or TGW? If it's a single account and low complexity, peering is fastest. If they want future scale (multi-account), TGW.

maria-se: I'm leaning peering for POC timebox. I'll tighten pricing: peering+interface endpoints = no infra fee; dedicated-proxy path = +1 week + one-time setup fee. I'll send numbers in next hour.

ida-security: I'll prepare the questionnaire answers and the one-page diagram. @sarah.ae once you confirm peering for the POC I'll sign off with the minimal rules.

sarah.ae: Confirmed: start with VPC peering flow for the POC, request preserved-srcip via co-located proxy later if Atlas insists. I'll share contact from their network team. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Deployment checklist created: JOB-4521 (private-peering-atlashealth). Assigned: kyle-net, ops-oncall. ETA: 48-72 hours for peering + SGs.

kyle-net: I'll draft the peering runbook + SG template and drop it here. If anyone has preapproved templates, tag me.

maria-se: Sending POC quote now.

ida-security: Tagging compliance docs here: https://redwood.example.com/security/poc-checklist — will update with Atlas CIDRs once received.

sarah.ae: Great, thanks everyone. I'll loop in Atlas netops and book a short handoff call after we drop the runbook.
